Render a block result, dispatching on the result's class

Source: R/html-page.R, R/result-output.R
block_result_output.Rd

block_output() dispatches on the BLOCK, which is the right hinge for a block that always draws the same kind of thing. A function or code block draws whatever its code returned, so the thing worth dispatching on is the RESULT: a data frame, a gt table, a ggplot, a package's own table class.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'html_page'
block_result_output(result, block, session, ...)

block_result_output(result, block, session, ...)

# Default S3 method
block_result_output(result, block, session, ...)

Arguments

result

The block's evaluated result.

block

The block object.

session

The block's Shiny module session.

...

Passed to methods.

Value

A shiny render function, as blockr.core::block_output() requires.

Details

The default method is render_dynamic_output(), the type switch this package has always used, so adding this generic changes nothing on its own. It exists so another package can teach a function block to draw its own object without that object's renderer having to live here – and, unlike an htmltools::as.tags() method, a method here receives the block's module session. That is what a renderer needs to namespace an element id, register a downloadHandler on session$output, or observe a click on session$input.

For example, a package with its own table class can register a method that draws the table through blockr.viz's renderer rather than through gt.

Called on every re-evaluation

blockr.core re-runs block_output() whenever the block's result changes (output_render_observer()). Assigning to session$output replaces the output and can be done on every call. An observer must be created once per block and not once per call, so a method keeps a note that it has made them.

That note, and any state the method keeps with it, has to end with the block. blockr.core destroys a block's session when the block is removed (session$destroy()). The observers, outputs and reactive values made in it are then gone, and Shiny refuses every later read or write of them. session$userData is shared by the whole Shiny session and is not cleared, so a note kept there is still found when a block is added again under the same id. Remove it in session$onDestroy():

key <- paste0("my_table:", session$ns(""))
if (is.null(session$userData[[key]])) {
  session$userData[[key]] <- TRUE
  session$onDestroy(function() session$userData[[key]] <- NULL)
  shiny::observeEvent(session$input$row, my_click(session$input$row))
}

Updating in place

The function a method returns replaces the block's output, so the browser draws the result again on every evaluation and what the user did to it (a scroll position, a search text) is lost. A result class that can change what it has on screen also registers a block_result_update() method.

The head row

A method can put its own tools, such as a download button, into the block's head row and give the block's sentence a title with result_head(). It reads the title, subtitle and caption now on screen with result_titles().

See also

block_result_update()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In a package with its own table class `my_table`:
block_result_output.my_table <- function(result, block, session, ...) {
  shiny::renderUI(draw_my_table(result))
}
} # }
